claims.text: Enhanced hydrogen spillover mediated by oxygen vacancies at a CeO2–platinum-group-metal interface governs ethanol-oxidation activity.
Enhanced hydrogen spillover governs ethanol-oxidation selectivity.
Enhanced hydrogen spillover governs catalyst durability during ethanol oxidation.
Conventional carbon-supported platinum-group-metal nanoparticles have minimal inherent oxygen vacancies and negligible spillover effects.
CeO2 nanorods possess abundant oxygen vacancies.
The oxygen-vacancy-rich, readily reducible character of CeO2 nanorods promotes hydrogen spillover.
Interfacial oxygen vacancies facilitate hydrogen or proton spillover to the metal nanoparticles.
Hydrogen spillover can involve migration of dissociated hydrogen from noble-metal nanoparticles onto a reducible oxide through coupled proton and electron transfer.
Hydrogen spillover stabilizes ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Hydrogen spillover stabilizes transition states required for complete ethanol oxidation.
The relevant complete ethanol-oxidation pathway transfers 12 electrons and 12 protons.
CeO2-nanorod-supported catalysts will exhibit higher ethanol-oxidation turnover frequencies than carbon-supported catalysts.
CeO2-nanorod-supported catalysts will exhibit lower ethanol-oxidation overpotentials than carbon-supported catalysts.
CeO2-nanorod-supported catalysts will have improved ethanol-oxidation selectivity relative to carbon-supported catalysts.
CeO2-nanorod-supported catalysts will be more durable than carbon-supported catalysts during ethanol oxidation.
The CeO2-supported catalyst will show enhanced interfacial proton dynamics relative to the carbon-supported catalyst.
The CeO2-supported catalyst will have lower metal–support charge-transfer resistance than the carbon-supported catalyst.
The proposed spillover mechanism is operative during ethanol oxidation in alkaline electrolyte at 25–60 °C.
Acidic environments diminish CeO2 reducibility or disrupt the proposed spillover mechanism.
Annealing the CeO2 nanorods will reduce their oxygen-vacancy concentration.

contradictions.description: The structural-mediator field describes spillover toward the metal nanoparticles, whereas the mechanism describes dissociated hydrogen migrating from the metal nanoparticles. The cited evidence supports the latter metal-to-support direction.
